passage:
Thursday, 11 p.m.
Skipped the seminar again. I got as far as the door, saw the chairs in a circle, and turned back. Ate lunch on the stairs behind the library so nobody would see me eating alone, which is silly, because that's exactly what I was doing. Ira from my class asked if I wanted to be in her group for the project. I said I already had one. I don't. On the walk back I called myself a coward about twenty times. It's week nine and I haven't made one friend. There's a poster outside the mess about the student counselling centre, free and private. I've walked past it every day. Tomorrow I'm going to write down the timings. Maybe even go in.
Yamini

qa.a: On the stairs behind the library.

qa.q: What does the name-calling on the walk back show about how Yamini feels?
qa.a: Yamini is lonely and harsh with self-criticism, blaming instead of comforting.

qa.q: What step does Yamini plan for tomorrow, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Writing down the counselling centre timings and maybe going in; seeking help early can make a real difference.

qa.q: How might Ira feel after hearing Yamini already had a group?
qa.a: Ira may feel a little rebuffed, not knowing the truth, and might not ask again unless Yamini reaches out.

grounding: A student who skips seminars, eats alone and refuses group work because being watched feels unbearable plans to visit the counselling centre.

Damini: how's week five? made friends yet?
Jasleen: not really
Jasleen: I dropped out of the drama club before the first meeting
Damini: I thought you loved theatre
Jasleen: I do. I just can't stand everyone looking at me. I eat in my room now
Damini: every meal?
Jasleen: mostly. I said no to the group project too. I'll do a solo one
Damini: that sounds really lonely, Jas
Jasleen: it is. and then I think, what's wrong with me
Damini: nothing's wrong with you. but this is getting bigger. does your college have a counsellor?
Jasleen: there's a wellness centre
Damini: can you book something this week? I'll stay on the phone while you fill the form
Jasleen: ok. now?
Damini: now.

qa.q: Which club did Jasleen drop out of?
qa.a: The drama club, before the first meeting.

qa.q: What does Jasleen think after admitting the loneliness?
qa.a: Jasleen thinks something must be wrong, turning the loneliness into self-criticism.

qa.q: What choice did Damini make once the pattern was clear?
qa.a: Damini said nothing was wrong with Jasleen, named that it was getting bigger, and stayed on the phone while Jasleen booked the wellness centre.

qa.q: How might Damini feel reading "I eat in my room now"?
qa.a: Damini is likely worried and sad, which is why the next question is "every meal?"
